studies.title: Effect of a breathing mask on type 2 mediator responses to subzero exercise in individuals without asthma.
studies.authors: Hanstock, Helen, Ainegren, Mats, Andersson, Erik P, Bäckebjörk, Ella et al.
studies.abstract: Current evidence suggests that heat and moisture-exchanging breathing masks (HME) protect against exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB). We aimed to explore whether mast cell mediator release following exercise in subzero conditions is affected by the use of an HME. To this end, 23 healthy, recreational-competitive endurance athletes aged 18-53 years without asthma performed a 30-min warm-up followed by a 4-min maximal, self-paced running time trial, with and without HME, in -15 °C. Concentrations of leukotriene E LTE₄ decreased after the 4-min maximal exercise test (p < 0.001), with no significant interaction with HME use. There was no effect of exercise alone nor HME on 11β-PGF2α responses to exercise. Taken together, we observed limited evidence of type 2 inflammation in healthy participants after brief, high-intensity exercise in the cold, with and without use of an HME. As the biomarker outcomes reported here were secondary and not powered in advance, these exploratory findings in a healthy cohort warrant further investigation using more robust airway challenges to better understand early airway responses and the potential for preventative strategies in athletes. studies.title: A pectic polysaccharide from Lonicera japonica alleviates DNCB-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation associated with gut microbial and metabolic alterations and reduced cutaneous JAK2/STAT3 activation and Th17 responses.
studies.authors: Jin, Mingzhu, Hu, Yue, Ding, Mengmeng, Cheng, Jiayue et al.
studies.abstract: Lonicera japonica Thunb. (Jin Yin Hua) is a traditional medicinal herb widely used in East Asia for inflammatory disorders and is commonly included in herbal prescriptions for atopic dermatitis (AD). WLJP-025p, a homogeneous pectic polysaccharide isolated from Lonicera japonica, has shown anti-inflammatory and anti-AD potential, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of WLJP-025p on DNCB-induced AD-like dermatitis in mice and to investigate associated changes in epidermal barrier dysfunction, Th17/IL-17A-associated inflammation, JAK2/STAT3 signaling, and gut microbial and metabolic profiles. An AD-like mouse model was established in BALB/c mice by repeated application of 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB). WLJP-025p was orally administered at 30 or 60 mg/kg during the challenge phase, and topical dexamethasone was used as a reference anti-inflammatory control. Disease severity was assessed by skin appearance, dermatitis score, ear thickness, serum biomarkers, and histopathological examination. Skin barrier and inflammation-related proteins were evaluated by immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. Colonic injury was examined by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Alcian blue-periodic acid-Schiff (AB-PAS) staining. Fecal metagenomic and metabolomic analyses were conducted to characterize gut microbial and metabolic changes. WLJP-025p significantly alleviated DNCB-induced AD-like lesions, as evidenced by reduced erythema, scaling, excoriation, ear swelling, dermatitis scores, epidermal hyperplasia, and mast cell infiltration. WLJP-025p decreased serum IgE, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-17A levels. It restored filaggrin (FLG) expression and suppressed thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) expression in skin lesions, indicating improved epidermal barrier function. WLJP-025p also reduced the proportions of splenic CD3 WLJP-025p exerted protective effects against DNCB-induced AD-like dermatitis. Treatment was accompanied by restoration of epidermal barrier-related markers, reduced JAK2/STAT3 activation and Th17/IL-17A-associated inflammatory signaling, improved gut barrier integrity, and alterations in gut microbial and fecal metabolite profiles. These findings indicate that oral WLJP-025p treatment is associated with concurrent intestinal and cutaneous changes in this AD-like model.

studies.title: The new revolution in the treatment of chronic urticaria, present and future of an effective and safe approach.
studies.journal: Italian journal of dermatology and venereology
studies.authors: Giménez-Arnau, Ana M, Barei, Francesca, Salman, Andaç
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a heterogeneous mast cell-driven disease associated with a substantial burden on patients' quality of life. Although most patients achieve disease control with guideline-recommended therapies, a relevant proportion remains refractory, highlighting important unmet needs. This narrative review summarizes current, emerging, and investigational treatments for CSU, discussing them with a pathogenesis-driven and endotype-oriented approach. Established therapies, including second-generation H1-antihistamines and omalizumab, are discussed alongside recently approved and upcoming agents such as dupilumab and Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors, particularly remibrutinib. In addition, novel strategies targeting mast cell survival and activation (antireceptor tyrosine kinase therapies), intracellular signaling pathways (Janus Kinase and Tyrosine kinase 2inhibitors), immunoglobulin E-independent activation (Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 antagonists), and next-generation anti-immunoglobulin E antibodies are reviewed. Beyond symptom control, the concepts of complete disease control, remission, relapse, and disease modification are examined. The evolving therapeutic landscape of CSU is expected to enable a more personalized management, with the potential to achieve sustained remission and, ultimately, disease modification in selected patients.

studies.title: Perioperative Management of Coexisting Mast Cell Activation Syndrome and Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility: A Case Report and Novel Approach to Local Analgesia.
studies.authors: Gearing, Peter Francis, Nack, Thomas, Liyanage, Dinuk, Martis, Walston Reginald et al.
studies.abstract: The coexistence of mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) and malignant hyperthermia (MH) presents a significant perioperative challenge due to combined risks of anaphylaxis and anaesthesia-related hypermetabolic crisis. We describe the successful anaesthetic management of a man in his 60 s with confirmed MCAS and a strong family history of MH who underwent excision of multiple malignant cutaneous lesions. A structured perioperative strategy incorporating immunological optimisation with omalizumab, strict trigger avoidance, dexmedetomidine and remifentanil procedural sedation, prophylactic corticosteroids and a controlled low-dose adrenaline infusion enabled safe completion of surgery without complication. In the absence of tolerated local anaesthetic agents, dilute adrenaline infiltration was used as an adjunct to improve procedural tolerability. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary planning and individualised perioperative strategy in patients with high-risk perioperative profiles.

studies.title: High Level of Component C1q Binding Protein (C1QBP) is Associated With Poor Prognosis and Dysfunction of Mast Cells in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
studies.authors: Li, Wei, Huang, Guangnan, Zeng, Lizhong, Dang, Wenhui et al.
studies.abstract: Component C1q binding protein (C1QBP) is known as an important regulator of mitochondrial plasticity and is involved in antitumor immune response in cancers. Nevertheless, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) still remains largely unknown. C1QBP expression in LUAD and adjacent normal samples was compared by Wilcoxon test, and the corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to estimate its diagnostic value. Associations between C1QBP expression levels and different clinical traits were analyzed by chi-square test; K-M curves were applied for analyzing survival differences, and univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were employed to construct the C1QBP-related nomogram model. Furthermore, GSEA and immune analysis were performed to explore the mechanism. Finally, rhC1QBP was applied to cultured mast cells in vivo to investigate its regulatory effect on mast cell dysfunction, and sh-C1QBP was injected into LUAD xenograft mice to explore the effect of C1QBP knockdown on tumor growth in vivo. The C1QBP expression level, with a preferable diagnosis effect, was significantly different between LUAD and normal samples, and was notably interrelated with gender, TNM stage, and Fustat in LUAD patients. LUAD patients with high C1QBP levels displayed lower survival rates. Our nomogram based on C1QBP expression and T stage displayed decent prediction capability. There was a significant difference in C1QBP expression in plasma cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), activated CD4 memory T cells, resting mast cells, and eosinophils between LUAD patients and the controls. Upregulation of C1QBP with rhC1QBP treatment promoted mast cell ferroptosis through interacting with the Cullin3 protein. While Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor, counteracted rhC1QBP induced ferroptosis in mast cells. Knockdown of C1QBP inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mice. C1QBP may be a promising potential prognostic biomarker in LUAD and a potential therapeutic target by affecting the immune microenvironment of LUAD patients.

studies.authors: Yu, Sunrui, Xu, Duojia, Hua, Yuting, Mo, Hangfeng et al.
studies.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis. Our study aims to investigate isonicotinylation (Kinic)-associated signature modulatory patterns in mast cells and DMD pathogenesis. We first performed integrated bioinformatic methods, such as WGCNA, GSVA, and CIBERSORT to identify Kinic and mast cell (KM)-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in DMD patient muscle bulk profiles (GSE38417 and GSE109178). Next, consensus clustering and assembling machine learning pipeline identified KM-associated diagnostic model and molecular subgroups in training the DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE6011), and then, diagnostic model performance was examined in the independent DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE32720). In addition, SHAP analysis decoded the main contributor in KM-associated diagnostic model construction, and contributor molecular and immune characters in DMD were estimated in GSE6011 and the DMD mouse muscle single-cell transcriptomic dataset (GSE213925) assisted by computational virtual cells. In addition, the deep learning framework and network pharmacology identified the drug synergy strategy for the treatment of DMD. Finally, the KM-associated molecular patterns can potentially guide the diagnostic and molecular stratification for DMD patients. USP18 can be considered an upregulated and mast cell-distributed hub gene involved in pathogenesis of DMD. In addition, finafloxacin with BRD-K10482608 can be considered two potential therapeutic candidates for DMD patient clinical applications. Our investigation described a novel forecasting and therapeutic model for DMD patients, which potentially enhances DMD patient clinical translation.

studies.title: Beyond Neuroinflammation: Targeting the Microbe-Barrier-Brain Axis Through Precision Nutrition in Neurological Long COVID (Neuro-PASC).
studies.authors: Velázquez De Castro-Bono, Amador, Castro-Luna, Gracia, Guil-Guerrero, José Luis
studies.abstract: Post-acute Neurological Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Neuro-PASC) contribute substantially to Long COVID-related disability, with cognitive impairment, chronic fatigue, dysautonomia, and neuropsychiatric symptoms among its most debilitating manifestations. Although its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood, evidence implicates persistent immune activation, intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbiota dysbiosis, microbiome-derived metabolic alterations, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroimmune interactions in sustaining neuroinflammation and neurological impairment. This narrative review examines precision nutrition as a potential pathway-oriented strategy for Neuro-PASC. We synthesise evidence linking the gut microbiota, intestinal permeability, immunometabolic pathways, mitochondrial function, and neurological outcomes, while evaluating nutritional interventions targeting these mechanisms. We focus on candidate biomarkers, including serum zonulin, fatty acid-binding protein 2 (FABP2), faecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio, which may support patient stratification and personalised nutritional strategies. We also propose a stepwise framework involving dietary stabilisation, functional foods, targeted supplementation, and microbiome-based interventions, alongside practical considerations for post-exertional symptom exacerbation, dysautonomia, and mast cell-related symptoms. Finally, we identify priorities for future research, including multi-omics integration, artificial intelligence, digital health, and biomarker-stratified randomised controlled trials. Because current evidence remains predominantly observational and mechanistic, precision nutrition should be considered a complementary strategy requiring rigorous clinical validation.

studies.title: Somatic Blood Mosaicism and Psychiatric Disease: Current Evidence and Causal Limits.
studies.authors: Belbe, Andrada-Adelaida, Pîrlog, Lorin-Manuel, Pilatec, Alissia-Nicoleta, Militaru, Mariela-Sanda et al.
studies.abstract: Somatic blood mosaicism is an established feature of ageing and a heterogeneous marker of haematologic cancer and inflammatory and vascular risk, but its psychiatric evidence base remains small. This structured critical narrative review evaluates mutation-defined clonal haematopoiesis, clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), autosomal mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs), and sex-chromosome loss while separating probable developmental mosaicism from adult-acquired blood clonality. Direct human evidence comprises seven methodologically heterogeneous studies. Psychiatric CHIP findings rely mainly on one prospective UK Biobank cohort of 360,451 participants, in which CHIP was associated with any incident psychiatric disorder (hazard ratio 1.15), particularly major depressive and substance-use disorders. Separate studies report excess mosaic losses in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and autosomal or X-chromosome mosaicism in suicide. Clone-size gradients and lesion-specific findings add biological structure, but do not provide independent replication. Most mechanistic support comes from cardiovascular, stroke and neurodegenerative research: mutant myeloid cells can alter inflammasome signalling, endothelial function, thrombosis and tissue macrophage behaviour. These pathways make indirect brain effects plausible without establishing a psychiatric mechanism. Blood detection also cannot date a mosaic event or demonstrate the same clone in neural tissue. Taken together, the available evidence supports somatic blood mosaicism as a potentially informative marker of psychiatric heterogeneity and shared inflammatory, vascular and ageing-related biology, but does not establish a causal blood-clone-to-brain pathway. Routine psychiatric screening for CHIP or mCAs is therefore not currently justified. The immediate research priority is independent replication in longitudinal cohorts with repeated sequencing, detailed exposure and treatment histories, and direct testing of inflammatory, vascular and neuroimaging intermediates capable of distinguishing cause, consequence and shared risk.

studies.title: Colonic Mast Cell Density and Diarrhoea: Evidence Against a Threshold Effect in Biopsies From 3508 Patients.
studies.authors: Langreiter, Marlena, Genta, Robert M, Schreiner, Philipp
studies.abstract: Elevated mast cell (MC) counts in colonic biopsies are frequently observed in patients with chronic diarrhoea or unspecific abdominal symptoms, potentially leading to a diagnosis of mast cell activation syndrome. However, the clinical relevance of MC quantification in this setting remains controversial. This study aimed to determine the proportion of patients with elevated MC counts who presented with diarrhoea compared to those with normal counts. As a secondary endpoint, we assessed how often MC quantification was performed and what the underlying clinical indications were. We analysed a large US national pathology database with 3.3 million colonoscopies performed between January 2009 and December 2023. Screening colonoscopies for colon cancer detection were excluded. For patients with multiple colonoscopies, only the first procedure was included. This resulted in a total of 2,059,147 colonoscopies. Colonic mast cells were evaluated in 3508 reports (0.17%). In 1167 cases the report contained either the expressions indicating increased MC, or a MC count > 20 MC/high power field (hpf). Diarrhoea was present in 58.3%, 54.1%, 54.7%, 50.0% and 33.3% of patients with MC count of < 20/hpf, 20-39/hpf, 40-59/hpf, 60-98/hpf and ≥ 99/hpf, respectively. These data do not show a relationship between diarrhoea and elevated MC in the colonic mucosa. Therefore, we suggest that the incorporation of MC quantification into the histologic evaluation of colonoscopic biopsies obtained for common GI indications may not be warranted.

studies.title: Shared mediators, divergent networks: a tissue-response hypothesis for discordant phenotypes in chronic spontaneous urticaria and atopic dermatitis.
studies.authors: Ye, Young-Min, Hide, Michihiro
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are pruritic inflammatory skin diseases that share partly overlapping mast-cell-related pathways, including IgE/FcεRI signaling, type 2 inflammation, neuroimmune signaling, and lipid mediator pathways. Yet they usually produce distinct phenotypes: transient wheals and angioedema in CSU and persistent eczematous lesions with inflammation in AD. Whether disease activity in the two conditions fluctuates concordantly or independently within the same patient has not been directly tested. This Perspective proposes that phenotypic divergence reflects the tissue-response network in which mast cell activation is embedded rather than mediator identity alone. In CSU, autoimmune and autoallergic FcεRI-dependent activation, MRGPRX2-related neuropeptide pathways, coagulation/fibrinolysis-C5a signaling, and platelet-activating factor (PAF)/lipid mediators may preferentially converge on mast cells and basophils poised for rapid degranulation within the dermal vascular/perivascular unit. This network favors histamine bursts, endothelial hyperpermeability, neurovascular itch, and feedback-limited wheal formation. In AD, mast cells are embedded in a barrier-disrupted, alarmin-rich neuroepidermal niche, producing a multicellular inflammatory network involving keratinocyte activation, cytokine and chemokine production, neuronal sensitization, itch-scratch cycling, and tissue remodeling, although degranulation and vascular effects may also occur. Neuropeptides and PAF illustrate how shared mediators may be preferentially routed toward vascular leakage in CSU or neuroepidermal inflammatory amplification in AD. This tissue-addressed mast cell output model is proposed as a testable hypothesis for how overlapping inflammatory mediators may generate feedback-limited vascular whealing in CSU but sustained neuroepidermal inflammation in AD. The model emphasizes that shared pathways are preferentially weighted toward different tissue-level outcomes in CSU and AD.

studies.title: IL-33/ST2 signalling in pediatric food allergy and eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review of human and preclinical evidence.
studies.authors: Grama, Monica, Săsăran, Maria Oana, Stan Muntean, Ana, Coman, Delia et al.
studies.abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is an epithelial-derived member of the IL-1 cytokine family that functions as an alarmin and signals through the ST2 receptor, upstream of type 2 inflammation. Together with thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) and IL-25, it constitutes an epithelial alarmin triad that orchestrates barrier-related immune responses. Despite substantial mechanistic data, the specific role of IL-33 as a biomarker and therapeutic target in pediatric food-related allergic disease remains insufficiently defined. This systematic review aims to synthesize current evidence on serum and tissue IL-33 in pediatric IgE-mediated food allergy and eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders (EGIDs), to delineate its association with disease severity, clinical phenotype and oral immunotherapy (OIT) outcomes, and to critically appraise the IL-33/ST2 axis as a candidate biomarker and therapeutic target within the broader epithelial alarmin network. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus and the Cochrane Library (2010-2026) identified pediatric clinical studies quantifying IL-33 or IL-33/ST2 in food allergy or EGIDs, alongside murine and Fourteen studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria (four pediatric clinical cohorts, ten direct preclinical murine or IL-33 emerges as a context-dependent yet non-redundant component of the epithelial alarmin circuitry in pediatric food-related allergic disease, as candidate biomarker of epithelial inflammation in pediatric EGIDs. However, current clinical evidence is limited and requires validation in larger prospective cohorts.

studies.title: Cutaneous Mast Cells Contribute to the Analgesic Effect of Manual Therapy on CCD Rats.
studies.authors: Yu, Jiayang, Sun, Pingping, Xie, Dong, Zeng, Xinyu et al.
studies.abstract: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) commonly induces low back and leg pain. Manual therapy (MT) is effective in relieving such pain clinically, but its mechanism remains unclear. Given that acupoint regions are enriched with mast cells that respond to mechanical stimulation, this study explored whether MT alleviates CCD-evoked neuropathic pain and its association with the modulation of cutaneous mast cells. Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomized into sham, chronic compression of dorsal root ganglion (CCD), MT, and mast cell inhibition (MCI) groups. After CCD modeling, MT was administered at BL57 starting on day 4 for 14 days, while MCI received acupoint cromolyn sodium injection. Paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) was measured. Mast cell activation was assessed using immunofluorescence and toluidine blue staining. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), substance P (SP), Piezo1, and Piezo2 were determined via immunofluorescence; inflammatory cytokines and neurotransmitters by ELISA; expression of MAPK, Piezo1, and Piezo2 by qRT-PCR. MAPK expressions were also detected by Western blot. CCD reduced PWT from day 3, whereas MT significantly restored PWT from day 11. In skin, CCD increased mast cell activation, CGRP, SP, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-1β, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), and histamine (HA), all of which were attenuated by both interventions. In DRG, CCD elevated p-ERK, p-JNK, and p-p38 MAPK without altering total MAPK expression, and both interventions suppressed MAPK phosphorylation. Piezo2 was upregulated in CCD and reduced by MT and MCI in both tissues. In skin, Piezo1 remained unchanged, while in DRG, CCD downregulated Piezo1 significantly. MT can relieve CCD-induced mechanical allodynia, an effect associated with inhibited cutaneous mast cell activation, attenuated peripheral neuroinflammation, and reduced MAPK hyperphosphorylation in the DRG.

studies.title: Microbial serotonin signalling axes in irritable bowel syndrome: integrative molecular crosstalk among enterochromaffin cells, gut microbiota, neuroimmune circuits, and precision therapeutic engineering.
studies.authors: Mehra, Ravinder Kumar, Singh, Bhanu Pratap, Siddiqui, Shakir, Aldawsari, Mohammed F et al.
studies.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common, often disabling disorder of gut-brain interaction whose molecular basis remains incompletely defined, leaving diagnosis largely symptom-based and treatment largely non-mechanistic. We argue that the serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; hereafter 5-HT, the primary term used throughout, with "serotonin" retained in less technical contexts) signalling axis-positioned at the interface of the gut microbiota, enterochromaffin (EC) cells, enteric neurons, and the mucosal immune system-is a central, unifying integrator of IBS pathophysiology, and that reframing IBS around this axis offers a route toward mechanism-based subtyping and therapy. We first synthesise how microbiota-driven tryptophan metabolism, short-chain fatty acid and secondary bile acid signalling, and epigenetic regulation of tryptophan hydroxylase 1 (TPH1) shape EC-cell serotonin output, before examining the neuroimmune consequences of dysregulated serotonin secretion-mast cell activation, macrophage polarisation, neurogenic inflammation-and the microbiota-serotonin-gut-brain connectome linking vagal afferent signalling, blood-brain barrier permeability, and central neurotransmitter networks. We then discuss molecular stratification of IBS subtypes through serotonergic endotyping-incorporating SLC6A4 and TPH1 polymorphisms, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics-and critically evaluate next-generation therapeutic strategies, including engineered probiotic chassis, CRISPR-mediated microbial editing, and AI-guided nanomedicine, distinguishing proof-of-concept findings from clinically validated approaches. We conclude that reconceptualising IBS as a disorder of disrupted microbial serotonergic ecosystems, rather than a purely symptom-defined syndrome, offers a coherent and testable framework for biomarker discovery and precision, mechanism-directed therapy, while highlighting the causal-directionality and clinical-translation gaps that must be closed before this framework can be applied at the bedside.

studies.title: Enhancing Surface Icephobic Performance via Spontaneous Fracture Characteristics of Ice Crystals Regulated by Structural Scale Under Shear Flow Conditions.
studies.authors: Jiang, Jiawei, Shen, Yizhou, Xu, Yangjiangshan, Xiang, Junxian et al.
studies.abstract: Icephobic surfaces are conventionally designed by minimizing ice adhesion; however, whether this strategy remains valid under aerodynamic shear remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that an external flow field fundamentally alters ice adhesion dynamics by inducing the spontaneous fracture and detachment of ice crystals through aerodynamic shear forces. The ice-substrate contact area is primarily determined by the initial droplet size prior to freezing, thereby governing the interfacial adhesion force. Furthermore, Ice detachment is controlled by a competitive interplay between the initial crystal size and its growth orientation, which together determine whether the aerodynamic loading is sufficient to overcome interfacial adhesion. Contrary to the conventional expectation that superhydrophobicity facilitates ice removal, the microstructural anchoring effect inherent to superhydrophobic surfaces impedes spontaneous ice detachment, resulting in substantially higher ice retention compared with conventional hydrophobic surfaces. By contrast, hydrophobic surfaces with nanoscale features exhibit a greater capacity to suppress runback-ice accumulation under flow than conventional hierarchical superhydrophobic surfaces. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for flow-induced spontaneous ice detachment and redefine an icephobicity design concept from minimizing adhesion toward controlling fracture dynamics.

studies.title: Overlapping Post-COVID Conditions: A Case of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome Triggered by Sequential Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infections.
studies.authors: Mayrink Magalhães, Virgínia R, Ribeiro Oliveira, Laura A, Lourenço, Adelina J, Ribeiro Camargos, Isabela et al.
studies.abstract: The rise in post-infectious syndromes following COVID-19, such as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), has become increasingly common in clinical practice, representing an emerging clinical challenge. This case highlights a possible clinical scenario involving the interaction between sequential viral infections - such as the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) - in triggering overlapping chronic conditions. This report presents the case of a patient who developed ME/CFS and POTS following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a prior history of EBV mononucleosis, and discusses the diagnostic, therapeutic, and pathophysiological implications. A 48-year-old woman with a history of mononucleosis in childhood developed persistent and disabling symptoms after COVID-19 in January 2022. She presented with extreme fatigue, orthostatic intolerance, paresthesia, cognitive dysfunction, and multisystem symptoms. After extensive investigation, she was diagnosed with ME/CFS (early 2023) and POTS (later that year). Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) was considered as a hypothesis during follow-up, but objective testing was not confirmatory. Management included pharmacological therapy (including low-dose naltrexone, duloxetine, and palmitoylethanolamide (PEA)), activity adjustments (pacing), and a multidisciplinary approach, with partial and fluctuating responses. This case illustrates how viral infections such as EBV and SARS-CoV-2 may act as sequential triggers in an individual clinical trajectory compatible with the development of ME/CFS and POTS. The symptomatic overlap, the lack of readily available objective biomarkers in this patient, and the need for a predominantly clinical and functional diagnostic approach in her evaluation highlight the complexity of these conditions. This experience also underscores the importance of continued efforts in research, clinical training, and integrated care models to improve the management of patients presenting with post-COVID conditions (PCC).

studies.abstract: Sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) is a safe and convenient treatment for allergic diseases, but it usually requires several years to achieve sufficient clinical benefit. Therefore, effective adjuvants are needed to enhance its efficacy and shorten the time required to achieve a therapeutic response. In this review, we summarize the rationale for using Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonists as adjuvants for SLIT and describe our recent preclinical findings with synthetic TLR4 agonist derivatives. We established a mouse model of sublingual administration using a small administration volume and a defined retention period after administration. Several TLR4 agonist derivatives enhanced allergen-specific serum IgG responses when administered with allergen. The adjuvant activity of one derivative was abolished in TLR4-knockout mice, indicating that its activity was dependent on TLR4 signaling. A selected derivative was further evaluated in combination with Japanese cedar pollen (JCP) extract. Co-administration of the derivative with JCP extract increased Cry j 1-specific IgG and IgA levels in serum and IgA levels in nasal lavage fluid. It also enhanced allergen-induced IL-10 production without substantially increasing IFN-γ or IL-4 production. Moreover, IgG from mice treated with the derivative and JCP extract more effectively inhibited allergen-induced mast cell degranulation than IgG from mice treated with JCP extract alone. These findings suggest that synthetic TLR4 agonists may enhance SLIT by promoting functional allergen-specific antibody responses. Further studies are needed to confirm their safety and clinical efficacy in humans.

studies.title: Systemic Mastocytosis With Associated Acute Myeloid Leukemia Identified After Induction Therapy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
studies.authors: Han, Joseph, Ghamsari, Farid, Yan, Jessica, Kim, Phyllis
studies.abstract: Systemic mastocytosis (SM) is a rare clonal mast cell disorder, with the vast majority of cases driven by activating KIT mutations, that can coexist with other myeloid hematologic malignancies. There are multiple subtypes of SM, one of which is SM with an associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN), which is the coexistence of SM and a separate neoplasm, often driven by a shared clonal origin. We report the case of a 48-year-old man who initially presented with profound leukocytosis, anemia, and thrombocytopenia and was subsequently diagnosed with AML. After undergoing induction chemotherapy, the patient was found to have less than 5% blasts but perivascular clusters of CD25-positive and CD117-positive cells on a day-14 bone marrow biopsy that were not previously seen, establishing the diagnosis of SM-AML. The patient is currently undergoing consolidation with consideration of allogeneic stem cell transplantation and potential additional maintenance therapy for SM. SM-AHN is a rare entity that has been reported in the literature; however, given its rarity, it does not have a well-established understanding of the drivers of malignancy, risk stratification, and prognostication, among other aspects that are better understood in more common malignancies. Here, we present a case of SM-AHN to contribute to the current literature and improve understanding of this rare entity.

studies.title: From disease activity scores to precision medicine: biomarkers and composite models for risk stratification in chronic spontaneous urticaria.
studies.authors: Elkhalifa, Shuayb, Abuzakouk, Mohamed
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria is a common, mast cell driven condition that presents with wheals, angioedema, or both, and a substantial proportion of patients remain inadequately controlled despite guideline-directed antihistamine therapy. The 2026 guideline has expanded the advanced-treatment options to include omalizumab, dupilumab and remibrutinib, while ciclosporin remains an alternative later-line immunosuppressive option, yet it is organised around treatment response rather than prognosis, so patients with difficult-to-control disease are often recognised only after months of sequential escalation. This narrative review examines the scoring systems and biomarkers available in urticaria and angioedema and considers whether they can support early risk stratification and help identify patients at increased risk of difficult-to-control disease. The validated instruments in routine use, namely the Urticaria Activity Score, the Urticaria Control Test, the Chronic Urticaria Quality of Life Questionnaire, and their angioedema counterparts, measure current disease activity, control, and quality of life rather than long term outcome. A separate body of work has described biomarkers associated with the autoimmune type IIb endotype and with response to omalizumab, including low total IgE, a high ratio of IgG anti-thyroid peroxidase to total IgE, basopenia, and raised inflammatory markers, although most of this evidence is associative rather than prospectively predictive. The distinction between markers of current burden, markers of prognosis, and markers of treatment response is emphasised. Composite models integrating clinical characteristics, patient-reported outcomes, and biomarkers represent a promising approach toward precision management of CSU, although no validated prognostic tool is currently available for routine clinical use.

studies.title: Endothelial injury and acute-phase inflammatory mediators converge to drive dengue severity.
studies.authors: Anshad, Abdul R, Atchaya, Muthuvel, Saravanan, Shanmugam, Murugesan, Amudhan et al.
studies.abstract: Severe dengue infection is characterized by endothelial injury and systemic inflammatory complications. To better understand the mechanisms underlying disease severity, we investigated a broad panel of circulating inflammatory and endothelial mediators in patients with clinical dengue infection. A prospective cross-sectional study was carried out involving 111 dengue patients and 42 healthy controls. Among the dengue cases, 85 were identified as primary, while 26 were classified as secondary dengue infections. Serum levels of endothelial markers (Ang-2, CXCL10, MCP1, and TRAIL), liver dysfunction and acute-phase markers (CRP, galectin 3, and serum amyloid protein), systemic inflammatory mediators (MIF, TNF-α, IL-1β), mast cell-derived proteases (chymase, tryptase), and tissue repair markers HGF, IL-10, IL-1Ra) were quantified using ELISA and Luminex multiplex assays. Correlations among serum analytes, severity indicators, and haematological markers were also explored. Several biomarkers, Ang-2, CXCL10, TRAIL, CRP, MIF, IL-1Ra, TNF-α, and chymase showed differential expression across severity groups, indicating coordinated endothelial and inflammatory activation. Stratification of patients with primary-secondary dengue also followed a similar pattern except IL-1β, which had significant differential expression across the cohorts. Ang-2 showed strong positive correlations with markers of hepatic dysfunction, including ALT, AST, and bilirubin, suggesting a link between endothelial injury and liver involvement. Severe dengue is driven by the coordinated activation of endothelial dysfunction, acute-phase responses, mast cell mediators, and counter-regulatory pathways. These processes collectively contribute to vascular leakage and organ injury, reinforcing the value of biomarkers such as Ang-2, CXCL10, CRP, and chymase for severity assessment.
